text:
kai: opened PR #5123 — added a tiny batch shim around kv prefetch to avoid the race we saw in production. can someone take a look? link: https://git.internal/repo/pulls/5123 :eyes:

alex: on it, will glance in a few. curious if this changes ordering semantics at all or just timing?

maria: i can review after lunch. is there a perf snapshot / benchmark in the PR?

kai: yeah added a microbench in the PR and a couple of e2e traces. summary: no throughput loss for normal workloads, ~0.3-0.6% extra p50 in synthetic tight loops but eliminates a stall path we saw under high prefix reuse. pasted the perf summary in the PR description.

santhosh: can we run the perf job versus main? i want an apples-to-apples run (same kernel build). i'll queue it but need the branch ref.

kai: branch is feature/kv-batch-shim. perf job flag: --compare=main. expect results in ~20m.

devops-bot: CI status: build ✅, unit tests ✅, integration tests ❌ (1 failure). See /ci/5123. failing test: tests/kv_cache/test_lru_eviction.py::test_evict_race_condition

alex: that test failure looks relevant. i'll reproduce locally, maybe a flake from timing. can someone add a repro snippet or a log from the CI run?

maria: if it's timing-sensitive we should add a short sleep in the test or make the assertion tolerant — but prefer to understand why shim changes scheduling. i'll review test and PR diff.

kai: repro snippet is in PR comments — small log shows two concurrent evict calls under heavy prefetch. adding the shim serializes the prefetch path so evict happens after writeback and avoids the assert.

julie: for rollout plan — if reviewers are comfortable, can we canary this on dedicated infra with 5% traffic and autoscale off? would like to observe real traffic latency and error rates before wide rollout.

santhosh: yes canary sounds good. also want a perf job that uses a long prefix distribution (more kv hits) to check p99 tail.

alex: local reproduce shows the test failing intermittently on master too (timing), so I created a small test-fix branch that makes the assertion resilient. pushing patch to PR as suggestion.

kai: thanks. i've pushed an update that incorporates alex's test-fix and added a comment about the canary plan. requested reviews from @maria @santhosh @alex.

maria: PTAL done — left one minor nit about a comment. overall LGTM once the integration test passes. :thumbsup:

santhosh: perf compare finished: p50 +0.4%, p95 +0.9%, p99 +1.2% on synthetic tight-ll tests; on real traffic simulation p50 unchanged, p95 +0.3%. logs attached in PR.

kai: thanks — numbers look acceptable. i'll wait for green CI then schedule canary deploy tomorrow at 09:00 PT. if no regressions after 2 hours we'll promote.

devops-bot: CI status: integration tests ✅.

julie: great, please add a short rollout note to the release channel when canary starts. include rollback steps.

kai: will do. thanks everyone. :sparkles:
